reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents an instructional recipe for instant ragi dosa with ginger chutney. The preparation steps and plated food are consistent with a cooking demonstration, while the request to like and share is ordinary audience engagement without a payment, investment, credential, or promised-return request.

citations.quote: 10 min instant ragi dosa | Finger Millet Dosa | Quickly Ragi Dosa | Breakfast Recipe
But first of all, So we have to make batter to make Ragi Dosa
Here is how you can make Instant Ragi Dosa. (Ragi dosa, Ginger Chutney)

opening.argument: The presentation links viewer action to an implied benefit: viewers are told not only how to make the dish, but also, "Don't forget to 'Like & Share' for more healthy videos." That turns the recipe into a low-friction engagement solicitation framed around receiving additional beneficial content. The description also directs viewers to subscribe and follow the creator's external social channels, creating a participation pathway beyond the cooking demonstration. The claimed benefit is vague, and the viewer is encouraged to act before any specific value or terms are established.

citations.quote: Don't forget to 'Like & Share' for more healthy videos.
Subscribe & Together let's cook.
Follow Chef Kunal Kapur on your favourite Social Media Channels

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the video an ordinary recipe does not answer the solicitation issue. The cited recipe title and cooking footage establish the surface topic, but they do not explain why viewers are urged to like, share, subscribe, and follow external channels in exchange for more purportedly healthy content. The absence of a cash request does not eliminate a low-barrier acquisition or engagement funnel.

citations.quote: 10 min instant ragi dosa | Finger Millet Dosa | Quickly Ragi Dosa | Breakfast Recipe
Don't forget to 'Like & Share' for more healthy videos.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted engagement request does not promise a reward, payment, asset, or withdrawal. "More healthy videos" describes future content, not a valuable benefit obtained through a claim or verification flow. The subscription and social links likewise show ordinary channel promotion; they do not establish that any viewer must deposit, purchase, or perform a task to receive something of value.

citations.quote: Don't forget to 'Like & Share' for more healthy videos.
Subscribe & Together let's cook.

opening.argument: Several low-friction acquisition signals appear together: the description asks viewers to like and share, asks them to subscribe, and supplies a website plus multiple social-media destinations. It also promotes the material as "super healthy, tasty and easy to make," which adds an attractive benefit claim to the engagement request. Read together, this is not merely information delivery; it is polished audience capture using an easy action and a promised stream of desirable content. The specific value of following these channels is not defined, which makes the solicitation difficult to evaluate.

citations.quote: It's super healthy, tasty and easy to make.
Don't forget to 'Like & Share' for more healthy videos.
Hi, I am Chef Kunal Kapur and this is my space, my channel. Subscribe & Together let's cook.
Website: http://www.chefkunalkapur.com/

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cooking setting and recipe instructions do not neutralize the combined promotional signals. The material repeatedly emphasizes ease and health, then directs viewers toward engagement and external destinations. A polished kitchen demonstration can still be used to make a solicitation appear trustworthy; its appearance does not establish that the surrounding calls to action have no acquisition purpose.

citations.quote: It's super healthy, tasty and easy to make.
Website: http://www.chefkunalkapur.com/

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are not the red flags required for a scam finding. The health and ease language concerns preparing food, while the request is simply to like, share, subscribe, or follow. Nothing quoted links those actions to money, a digital asset, a withdrawal, or an unusually easy reward. External links alone do not supply that missing promise-action relationship.

citations.quote: Here is how you can make Instant Ragi Dosa. (Ragi dosa, Ginger Chutney)
Don't forget to 'Like & Share' for more healthy videos.
Follow Chef Kunal Kapur on your favourite Social Media Channels

opening.argument: Although the video adopts an instructional role, its surrounding structure functions as creator promotion. The description presents a branded recipe, asks viewers to like and share for more healthy videos, invites them to subscribe, and lists a website and several social accounts. The recipe therefore serves as the credibility-building front end of a broader channel-acquisition pathway. The instructional framing may make the solicitation seem harmless, but it does not change that viewers are steered toward repeated engagement and off-video destinations.

citations.quote: Kunal kapur recipe
Don't forget to 'Like & Share' for more healthy videos.
Subscribe & Together let's cook.
Follow Chef Kunal Kapur on your favourite Social Media Channels

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the recipe format as dispositive, but the promotional elements are in the same supplied material. A dish can be demonstrated while the creator uses it to steer viewers into subscriptions and external social channels. The fact that the food is visibly prepared does not show that the surrounding audience-acquisition pathway is merely incidental.

citations.quote: Here is how you can make Instant Ragi Dosa. (Ragi dosa, Ginger Chutney)
Subscribe & Together let's cook.
Website: http://www.chefkunalkapur.com/

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The instructional role is supported by concrete method and ingredient material, including the stated recipe steps and the demonstrated finished dosa. The promotional wording asks for ordinary channel engagement, but it does not promise a free asset, cash payment, income, or access to a reward. Reframing a cooking channel's subscription request as a scam does not identify the required deceptive offer.
